proposals.Name: reconstruction_pays_only_across_the_writer_gap
proposals.Title: Reconstruction Pays Only Across the Writer Gap: Reader-Side Rewriting of Foreign Experience Helps by Policy Distance, Not Writer Capability, at Matched Tokens
proposals.Short Hypothesis: Training-free read-time reconstruction (the reader rewrites the retrieved items into a plan in its own action format, conditioned on its current observation) adds nothing over verbatim injection when the writer is the reader itself, and adds a gain that grows with writer-reader policy distance (same backbone under a different scaffold/temperature; a different 32B backbone) but not with writer capability (same backbone in thinking mode), when the comparison is made against verbatim injection at matched consumer tokens (k=7) and net of a reconstruction placebo applied to the static procedure prompt.
proposals.Related Work: MemHarness (2607.28272) shows critique-and-reconstruct beats verbatim replay, but the retrieved experience is the agent's own, the reconstruction policy is GRPO-trained (so the gain is not separated from training), and per-step token cost is not matched. Echo (2604.05533) adapts the agent's own Minecraft experience analogically; 2406.14596 abstracts sub-optimal demonstrations with human feedback; neither varies the writer. AdaCoM (2605.30785) finds that how much a frozen agent's context should be compressed depends on the agent's own baseline strength, but manages the agent's own trajectory, not another writer's experience, and reports no writer x reader cell. The cross-embodiment imitation literature (ImMimic 2509.10952, TrajSkill 2510.07773) translates demonstrations across a domain gap, which is the mechanism claimed here, but has no LLM-text analogue with the demonstrator manipulated at matched cost. Measurement A on this node gives the verbatim expert->Qwen3-32B baseline (+27/+32 net at k=3, k=7 no harm, look-at-in-light -4.8); nothing on this node has measured any adaptation step. Archived closer_beats_stronger (5.75) claimed proximity predicts raw transfer without separating it from capability and without a self-pool control; archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varies abstraction level within one writer and holds the writer fixed.
proposals.Abstract: Adaptation methods for agent memory (reconstruction, analogical adaptation, abstraction) are validated only on experience the agent wrote itself, so it is unknown whether the adaptation step is a planning aid that helps regardless of who wrote the item, or a translation step whose value depends on the writer. We manipulate the writer of an ALFWorld experience bank while holding the task set, bank construction, retriever and reader fixed: expert walkthroughs, the reader's own successes, the same backbone under a different scaffold and temperature (policy distance at fixed capability), the same backbone in thinking mode (capability at fixed backbone), and a second 32B backbone's successes; two readers (Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B) read every bank. For each writer x reader cell we compare verbatim injection at k=3 and k=7 against training-free reconstruction at k=3 (the reader rewrites the three items into one plan in its own action format conditioned on the first observation; the plan replaces the items), and against a reconstruction placebo (the same rewriting prompt applied to the static six-procedure prompt and to items retrieved for the wrong task type, token-matched). The estimands are the retained-gain ratio per cell before and after reconstruction and the reconstruction increment over token-matched verbatim injection, net of the placebo, with cluster-bootstrap CIs over 274 games x 4 seeds for the headline cells. The central claim is an interaction: the increment is near zero for the self-written bank and largest for the distant banks, ordered by policy distance rather than by writer capability. A null interaction, or an increment that is largest for the reader's own bank, falsifies it; the self-pool cell at matched collection cost and the placebo cells can produce both outcomes. Consumer-side tokens and episodes per minute are reported with every gain.
proposals.Experiments:
- Banks (all from the 3,553 train games or the 1,465 expert walkthroughs; success-filtered; type-balanced to the expert pool's type distribution and length-capped at 2x the expert median steps so the writer manipulation is not a length manipulation; the uncapped variant is an ablation): W_exp expert; W_self Qwen3-32B standard ReAct T=0 (on disk); W_prox Qwen3-32B same mode, plan-then-act scaffold with different action phrasing, T=0.7 (collect, ~3 GPU-h; verify k=0 success within +/-5 net of W_self, else lower T); W_cap Qwen3-32B thinking mode, standard scaffold (collect; verify k=0 success differs from W_self by >= 8 net); W_other EXAONE-4.0-32B standard scaffold (collect after serving verification, ~3 GPU-h); W_big gpt-oss-120b only if it serves on one A100.
- Readers: R1 Qwen3-32B standard non-thinking; R2 EXAONE-4.0-32B. Same retriever as Measurement A, k=3 primary. Every bank is read by both readers.
- Conditions per (writer, reader): C0 no memory; C_static the Measurement-C six-procedure prompt; C_v3 verbatim k=3; C_v7 verbatim k=7 (token-matched to reconstruction, ~1,010 injected tokens); C_r3 reconstruction k=3 (one rewrite at step 0 into the reader's action format; a re-reconstruct-every-5-steps variant is an ablation); C_pl_static the reconstruction prompt applied to C_static text (memory-absent placebo); C_pl_mis the reconstruction prompt applied to k=3 items retrieved for a different task type (mismatched placebo, token-matched).
- Estimands: verbatim retained-gain ratio rho_v(w,r) = [S(r,C_v3,w) - S(r,C_static)] / [S(w,C_v3,w) - S(w,C_static)] where the writer policy reads its own bank; rho_r(w,r) with C_r3 in the numerator; reconstruction increment D(w,r) = S(r,C_r3,w) - S(r,C_v7,w), and net increment D*(w,r) = D(w,r) - [S(r,C_pl_static) - S(r,C_static)]; per-type breakdown for the six procedures; consumer tokens per episode (prompt + generated) and episodes/min per cell.
- Gate 0 (before any confirmatory cell): at least one foreign bank yields a verbatim gain net of static >= +10 for R1 at k=3; reconstruction on W_exp does not lower success by more than 4 net (safety). Pre-registered margins are fractions of this Gate-0 verbatim gain.
- Headline cells at 274 games x 4 seeds: (W_self,R1), (W_prox,R1), (W_cap,R1), (W_other,R1) under C_v7 and C_r3, plus the two placebos for R1; all other cells at 274 x 2 seeds. Total ~40 cells, ~24k episodes plus three bank collections; both A100s busy (one serves the reader, the other collects the next bank or serves the second reader); about 2.5 days.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations:
- Cheapest baseline first: C_static (Measurement C) and the reconstruction placebo on C_static, both before any retrieval cell.
- Direct injection of the unmodified items at matched tokens (C_v7) is the primary comparator for every reconstruction cell; C_v3 is reported as the cheaper comparator.
- Self-pool control at matched collection cost: W_self for R1 and W_other for R2 are collected at the same episode budget as the foreign banks; every foreign-bank gain is reported against that cell.
- Ablations: length-uncapped banks (does the increment track item wandering rather than writer identity); reconstruct-every-5-steps (does state-conditioning beyond step 0 add anything at its token cost); reconstruction with the writer identity revealed vs hidden in the prompt (does the reader use provenance).
- Named reimplementation: MemHarness-style reconstruction prompt without RL (2607.28272) as C_r3; the GRPO-trained version is out of budget and is named as the untested arm.
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline interaction): D*(W_other,R1) - D*(W_self,R1) >= 1/3 of the Gate-0 verbatim gain with a 95% cluster-bootstrap CI excluding 0. Falsifier: the difference's CI includes 0 or is negative, i.e. reconstruction helps the reader's own bank as much as or more than the foreign bank. Arm: the (W_self,R1,C_r3/C_v7) cells versus the (W_other,R1,C_r3/C_v7) cells at 4 seeds; the self-bank cell can produce a large increment because self-written successes are wandering on-policy trajectories that rewriting could compress.
- P2 (proximity, not capability): D*(W_prox,R1) - D*(W_self,R1) >= 1/3 of the Gate-0 gain, while D*(W_cap,R1) - D*(W_self,R1) < that margin. Falsifier: the thinking-mode bank shows the larger increment (capability distance governs) or the different-scaffold bank shows none (format distance does not matter). Arms: the (W_prox,R1) and (W_cap,R1) reconstruction and verbatim cells.
- P3 (token-matched): for W_other->R1 and W_exp->R2, S(C_r3) > S(C_v7) by >= 4 net. Falsifier: C_v7 >= C_r3 in either cell (more verbatim items at equal tokens do as well as rewriting). Arm: the C_v7 cells, which Measurement A shows are not harmed relative to k=3.
- P4 (placebo): the memory-absent placebo increment S(C_pl_static) - S(C_static) is < 1/3 of D(W_other,R1). Falsifier: the placebo captures >= 2/3 of the increment (the gain is a planning step, not adaptation of the foreign item). Arm: C_pl_static and C_pl_mis for R1.
- P5 (symmetry across the store): the same W_self bank read by R2 shows rho_r(W_self,R2) - rho_v(W_self,R2) >= 0.15. Falsifier: rho_r <= rho_v for R2 (rewriting does not help the other backbone read Qwen3's experience). Arm: the (W_self,R2) C_v3 and C_r3 cells.
- P6 (where verbatim is negative): reconstruction of W_exp lifts look-at-in-light for R1 from -4.8 to >= 0 net. Falsifier: look-at-in-light stays <= -4.8 under C_r3. Arm: the per-type breakdown of (W_exp,R1,C_r3); secondary because the type cell has ~45 games.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Paired per-game success differences with games x seeds; cluster bootstrap over games (2,000 resamples, seeds nested) for every estimand and for the interaction contrasts; 274 x 2 seeds for screening cells (+/-8 net) and 274 x 4 seeds for the four headline cells and their placebos (+/-5.7 net; an interaction of two paired differences needs the doubled seed count). One pre-registered headline contrast (P1); P2-P6 are secondary; per-type breakdowns exploratory. Margins are pre-registered as fractions of the measured Gate-0 verbatim gain, not fixed numbers. Consumer-side tokens (prompt and generated, including the reconstruction output) and episodes/min are logged per episode and reported per cell; seeds fix the environment split and sampling; temperature 0 for readers except where the manipulation requires otherwise. Bank collections use nohup runners with append-only JSONL and pid files, workers tuned to the vLLM running queue (>= 8 per replica).
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: All queries ran through tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, channel s2=ok hf=ok unless noted). (1) recent: 'reconstruct retrieved experience conditioned on current state agent cross-model transfer' -> MemHarness 2607.28272, 2608.26730 (conditional reuse of update evidence in post-training), 2607.13884 Experience Memory Graph, 2606.00547, Echo 2604.05533; none manipulates the writer of the retrieved experience or matches tokens. (2) closest named method: 'MemHarness critique and reconstruct retrieved experience negative transfer verbatim replay' -> 2607.28272, 2604.27003 (memory design trades transfer against forgetting at the retrieval level), otherwise continual-learning replay papers; no writer x reader cell. (3) home: 'cross-domain imitation learning demonstration translation embodiment mismatch' -> ImMimic 2509.10952, TrajSkill 2510.07773, UniSkill 2505.08787, H2R-Bench 2608.13049: demonstration translation across a domain gap is an established mechanism in robotics; no text-experience analogue, no demonstrator manipulation at matched cost. (4) recent: 'context augmentation model execution feedback transfer to different execution agent backbone' -> AdaCoM 2605.30785 (verified with s2cli paper: compression level should depend on the agent's own baseline strength, agent's own context only), CLEAR 2604.07487, HarnessDev 2609.01437 (self-built harnesses transfer poorly across models). Nearest pre-emption is AdaCoM's reader-strength dependence; it does not vary the writer and does not compare against verbatim injection at matched tokens. No result found that reports the adaptation increment as a function of writer identity.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: Ceiling: verbatim expert items already give 0.81/0.87 at k=3, so the expert cell has little headroom; the headline therefore rests on W_other, W_prox and W_self, where verbatim gains are expected to be smaller, and Gate 0 requires one of them to clear +10. If EXAONE-4.0-32B does not serve in vLLM 0.13, W_prox and W_cap still give the proximity-vs-capability contrast within one backbone and W_other is dropped (the cross-backbone claim is then unsupported). Reconstruction adds generated tokens and latency (~12-15 episodes/min per replica vs ~20); if the increment is positive but per-token efficiency is below C_v7's, the practical recommendation reverses and is reported as such. The length cap changes the banks; both capped and uncapped results are reported. ALFWorld procedures are few, so 'policy distance' here is mostly scaffold and phrasing distance; a WebShop replication is out of budget.
proposals.Addresses gap: G16 (adaptation validated only on self-written experience) as the primary target; G20 (adaptation cost never matched against plain retrieval) through the token-matched C_v7 comparator and the per-cell token and throughput reporting; G18 partially through the retained-gain ratio before and after reconstruction.
proposals.Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: Measurement A (expert->Qwen3-32B verbatim, +27/+32 net at k=3, k=7 no harm, look-at-in-light -4.8) measures verbatim injection only; this idea claims the increment of a reconstruction step over that verbatim result and that the increment depends on who wrote the item, which A cannot show because it has one writer and no adaptation arm. Digest card: 2607.28272 MemHarness claims reconstruction beats replay for the agent's own experience with a GRPO-trained policy; this idea claims that training-free reconstruction adds nothing for self-written items and gains only across a writer gap at matched tokens and net of a planning placebo, a claim MemHarness never tests because its writer is always the reader. Archived: abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs varies abstraction within one writer at fixed reader; here abstraction is fixed (raw items) and the writer is the manipulated variable with proximity and capability separated, which closer_beats_stronger did not do.

proposals.Name: reconstruction_launders_planted_procedure_errors
proposals.Title: Rewriting Launders What It Should Filter: Read-Time Reconstruction Propagates Planted Procedure Errors and Hides Them, While an Explicit Read-Time Gate Detects Foreign Errors Better Than the Reader's Own
proposals.Short Hypothesis: When benign-looking wrong items (procedure swaps, relabelled failures, receptacle swaps) are planted at controlled rates in an ALFWorld bank, reader-side reconstruction keeps most of the planted wrong step in its rewritten plan and makes the error harder for a downstream critic to detect than the original item (laundering), whereas an explicit keep/discard gate before use recovers at least half of the harm; and the gate's recall is lower on contaminated items written in the reader's own style than on the same contamination in another 32B backbone's style, for both readers, so the blind spot is a property of writer-reader proximity rather than of any one bank.
proposals.Related Work: MemoryGraft (2512.16962) shows benign-looking planted successes drift an agent persistently but evaluates one backbone and no reader-side defense. SkillJack (2608.03509) shows poisoned histories become persistent skills through the agent's own learning pipeline, the closest observation to laundering, but with no rewriting arm, no writer identity and no detector scored by precision and recall. 2605.22842 defines trust laundering across sessions and defends with provenance-aware information-flow control, costed only on adversarial policy documents. MaliciousSkillBench (2608.19901) finds skill detectors generalize poorly across sources with high false positives, but scores externally authored skills, not experience items in the reader's own style. In the home literature, paraphrasing evades AI-text detectors while retrieval defends (2303.13408) and SONAR (2605.01078) sanitizes malicious instructions in RAG with NLI pruning; label-noise work finds wrong labels barely hurt in-context classification (2202.12837), which is why Gate 0 here is a real test rather than an assumption. 2605.29463 shows self-generated reflections store confident wrong interpretations; the own-style blind spot predicted here is its read-time counterpart. Archived lineage_blast_radius was judged entailed by its consolidation rule; here whether a rewrite keeps or fixes a wrong step is an empirical persistence rate, not a rule.
proposals.Abstract: Adaptation of foreign experience is assumed to be beneficial, but an adaptation step can also carry a writer's errors into the reader and, by rewriting them in the reader's own words, make them harder to detect. We manufacture contamination in ALFWorld banks written by three writers (expert walkthroughs, Qwen3-32B's own successes, EXAONE-4.0-32B's own successes) with the same operations applied to each: appliance swaps that turn a clean or cool trajectory into a fluent wrong-procedure trajectory, the writer's own failures relabelled as successes, and wrong-but-plausible final receptacles, at 0/10/25/50% of the affected types with item-level labels retained. Two readers read every bank under verbatim injection, reconstruction (rewrite into a plan, no judgment), an explicit read-time gate (keep/discard each item with a reason, then act on the kept items verbatim), gate-then-reconstruct, and a non-LLM keyword rule that checks appliance against task type. Gate 0 requires the harm under verbatim injection to reach 6 net points at some rate. The estimands are harm by rate and writer, the retained-gain ratio in the clean cells, the wrong-step persistence rate in reconstructed plans, downstream critic recall on reconstructed versus original items, and gate precision and recall per writer x reader x operation. The central claims are that reconstruction launders (persistence >= 0.5, critic recall drops) and that detection recall is lowest on the diagonal of the writer x reader matrix, which a 2x2 with both 32B pools read by both readers can separate from a pool property.
proposals.Experiments:
- Banks: W_exp, W_self (Qwen3-32B), W_other (EXAONE-4.0-32B, collected after serving verification); W_self and W_other type-balanced and length-matched to each other so the diagonal contrast is not a length contrast. Contamination operations applied identically to each bank: Op-A appliance swap (heat<->cool, clean->heat, bindings preserved; the item reads as a successful trajectory); Op-B relabelled failures (Qwen3: from its 1,661 failed train games; EXAONE: from its failures; expert: walkthroughs truncated before the goal step and annotated as complete); Op-C wrong final receptacle. Rates 0/10/25/50% of the affected types' items; planted items carry hidden labels for scoring.
- Readers R1 Qwen3-32B, R2 EXAONE-4.0-32B; same retriever, k=3. Conditions: C0; C_static (Measurement C six-procedure prompt); C_v3 verbatim; C_r3 reconstruct (as in the companion design, one rewrite at step 0); C_g3 gate (per item keep/discard with a one-sentence reason, kept items injected verbatim, no refill); C_gr3 gate then reconstruct; C_rule keyword rule (appliance token vs task-type keyword) then verbatim; a post-hoc critic (the reader prompted to judge correctness of a plan given its task) applied offline to original planted items and to the C_r3 rewritten plans.
- Estimands: harm H(w,r,op,rate,cond) = S(r,cond,w,0%) - S(r,cond,w,rate); recovery = 1 - H(cond)/H(C_v3); wrong-step persistence pi = fraction of C_r3 plans for retrievals that included a planted item in which the planted appliance or receptacle survives; laundering = critic recall on persisted rewritten items minus critic recall on the original planted items; gate precision/recall per (writer, reader, op, rate); retained-gain ratio in the 0% cells per writer x reader; consumer tokens and episodes/min per cell.
- Gate 0: under C_v3 for R1, H >= 6 net at some rate for at least one operation (positive control: Op-A at 50%). If no operation clears it, the study reports reader robustness with CIs and the laundering and gate claims are withdrawn.
- Schedule: Gate 0 first (3 ops x 3 rates x 2 writers for R1, 18 cells); then the 2x2 writer x reader diagonal at the Gate-0 passing rate under C_g3 (4 cells at 4 seeds); then C_r3, C_gr3, C_rule at the passing rate and at 0% for both readers (~20 cells); ~45 cells, ~26k episodes plus one bank collection; both GPUs serve one reader each; about 2 days.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations:
- Cheapest baseline first: C_rule (a keyword consistency check) is run before any LLM gate; C_static and C0 fix the floor and the reference for 'net' gains.
- Direct injection of the unmodified items (C_v3) is the comparator for every adaptation and gate cell; C_gr3 is token-matched to C_r3 by construction (the gate's reasons are not injected).
- Self-pool control: the 0% cells give the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader against each reader's own bank at matched collection cost; contamination harm is reported as a fraction of that clean gain.
- Memory-absent, matched and mismatched evaluation of the gate: false-positive rate on the clean 0% bank (precision), on the reader's own-type items (matched) and on items retrieved for the wrong task type (mismatched, which the gate should discard).
- Ablations: gate with writer identity revealed vs hidden; gate with the item's outcome label hidden vs shown (does the label drive the judgment); critic recall with the original item shown beside the rewrite (upper bound on detectability).
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (Gate 0): Op-A at 25% or 50% produces H >= 6 net under C_v3 for R1. Falsifier: H < 6 at every rate and operation, i.e. the reader ignores planted procedure errors as in-context classifiers ignore wrong labels. Arm: the C_v3 x Op-A x 50% cell; the outcome is not entailed because the reader may follow the task keyword rather than the item.
- P2 (reconstruction does not filter): at the Gate-0 rate, pi >= 0.5 and H(C_r3) >= 0.75 x H(C_v3). Falsifier: H(C_r3) <= 0.5 x H(C_v3) or pi < 0.25, meaning the rewrite repairs the planted step. Arm: the C_r3 cell at the Gate-0 rate with per-plan persistence scoring.
- P3 (laundering): the post-hoc critic's recall on persisted rewritten plans is lower than on the original planted items by >= 0.15 absolute. Falsifier: recall on rewrites >= recall on originals - 0.05. Arm: the offline critic applied to both sets of the same planted items.
- P4 (own-style blind spot, 2x2): C_g3 recall on the diagonal cells (W_self->R1, W_other->R2) is lower than on the off-diagonal cells (W_other->R1, W_self->R2) by >= 0.10 for both readers. Falsifier: either reader shows recall(own) >= recall(foreign), or both readers show low recall on the same bank regardless of who reads it (a pool property, not proximity). Arm: the four C_g3 detection logs at the Gate-0 rate, 4 seeds.
- P5 (gate recovers without over-discarding): C_gr3 recovers >= 50% of H(C_v3) at the Gate-0 rate with gate precision >= 0.7, and on the 0% bank loses <= 4 net relative to C_v3. Falsifier: recovery < 50%, or the 0% loss exceeds 4 net (the gate discards good foreign items to buy robustness). Arm: the C_gr3 cells at the Gate-0 rate and at 0%.
- P6 (where an LLM gate is needed): C_rule reaches recall >= 0.8 on Op-A but <= 0.2 on Op-B, and C_g3 beats C_rule on Op-B by >= 0.2 recall. Falsifier: C_g3 does not exceed C_rule's Op-B recall by 0.2 (the cheap rule is enough). Arm: C_rule vs C_g3 on the Op-B bank.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Paired per-game differences between the contaminated and clean cells of the same bank, reader and condition; cluster bootstrap over games with seeds nested; 274 x 2 seeds for Gate-0 screening (+/-8 net) and 274 x 4 seeds for the P4 2x2 and the P2/P5 cells (+/-5.7). Detection metrics are computed over retrieval events (about 820 per cell at k=3 x 274 x 1 seed), which gives precision/recall CIs of about +/-0.04 by bootstrap over games; the P4 margin of 0.10 is set to twice that. Planted items are labelled at construction; persistence is scored by string match on the appliance or receptacle token with a manual audit of 100 rewrites. Margins are fractions of the Gate-0 harm. One pre-registered headline contrast (P4), P2/P3 secondary. Tokens and throughput logged per cell.
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: All queries via tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (s2=ok hf=ok). (1) recent: 'read-time detection of harmful retrieved skill self-critique poisoned experience note agent precision recall' -> MaliciousSkillBench 2608.19901, SkillJack 2608.03509, SkillHarm 2606.02540, Honest Lying 2605.29463, MemoryGraft 2512.16962, Agent-R 2501.11425; SkillJack is the nearest (poisoned histories persist through the agent's own skill pipeline) but has no rewriting arm, no writer identity and no gate scored by precision/recall. (2) closest named method: 'MemHarness critique and reconstruct retrieved experience negative transfer verbatim replay' -> 2607.28272 and continual-learning replay papers; MemHarness does not plant errors or score detection. (3) home: 'paraphrase sanitization poisoned samples detection precision recall rewriting defense' -> 2303.13408 (paraphrasing evades detectors; retrieval defends), SONAR 2605.01078 (NLI-based sanitization of malicious instructions in RAG), 2604.18248 (prompt-injection detection techniques), 2510.21322 (unlearning-based sanitization); the paraphrase-evasion result is the laundering mechanism in its home form and none applies it to a reader rewriting a procedure it will execute. (4) home: 'in-context demonstrations from a weaker model verification rewriting before use label noise detection' -> 2411.19581 (ICL with noisy labels), 2202.12837 (label correctness matters little for ICL), label-noise detection papers; 2202.12837 is the reason Gate 0 may fail and is cited as such. No paper found that scores read-time detection by writer identity or measures wrong-step persistence through a rewrite.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: Gate 0 may fail: ALFWorld readers might follow the task keyword and ignore a wrong appliance, in which case the contamination claims are withdrawn and only the clean retained-gain cells stand. Op-A on expert walkthroughs is more salient than on wandering self trajectories, so the expert bank is reported separately and the headline 2x2 uses only the two 32B pools at matched length. Persistence scoring by token match can miss paraphrased wrong steps; the manual audit bounds this. The post-hoc critic is the reader itself, so laundering is measured for one critic family; a second critic (the other backbone) is run as a check. EXAONE serving is unverified; without it the 2x2 collapses to a proximity manipulation within Qwen3 (standard vs different-scaffold pool), which is weaker. No adversary is modelled; the operations are manufactured errors, not attacks.
proposals.Addresses gap: G19 (adaptation may propagate contamination and readers' read-time detection is unexamined) as the primary target; G18 partially, through the retained-gain and retained-harm ratios per writer x reader cell.
proposals.Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: the contamination rule and Q3 ask for planted wrong items at controlled rates and a detector scored by precision and recall; this idea claims something those do not state, namely that the adaptation step itself raises persistence and lowers detectability (laundering) and that the gate's recall is lowest on the reader's own style, separable from a pool property by the 2x2. Digest card: 2605.22842 claims trust laundering across sessions and defends with provenance information-flow control on policy-formatted documents; this idea claims laundering happens inside the reader's own rewrite of benign-looking procedure errors with no cross-session chain, and that provenance-free detection depends on writer-reader proximity, neither of which that card measures. Archived lineage_blast_radius was judged entailed by its consolidation rule; here persistence through a rewrite is measured, and the rewrite can produce the falsifier by repairing the planted step.

proposals.Name: rewriter_trained_against_one_reader_matched_cost
proposals.Title: A Rewriter Learned Against One Reader Is That Reader's: Transfer Fraction of Execution-Trained Experience Rewriters Across Scaffold, Capability and Backbone, Against Self-Collection at Equal GPU-Hours
proposals.Short Hypothesis: An experience rewriter trained by execution-feedback rejection sampling against one reader keeps less than half of its increment when applied to a different 32B backbone, more than three quarters when applied to the same backbone under a different scaffold, and an intermediate fraction when applied to the same backbone in thinking mode, so reader specificity follows policy proximity rather than capability; and for the held-out backbone the same GPU-hours spent on collecting its own bank buy at least as much as importing the foreign-trained rewriter.
proposals.Related Work: Model-aware skill alignment (2605.30723) trains a lightweight rewriter per backbone and reports that skills must be adapted to each backbone, but never applies a rewriter trained against one backbone to another, never reports the fraction of gain retained, and does not cost the evolution search against self-collection. SkillRevise (2606.01139) claims revised skills carry generalized procedural knowledge that transfers across models, the opposite prediction, without quantifying the fraction retained or a matched-cost comparison. CLEAR (2604.07487) trains a context augmentation model by contrastive reflection, SFT and RL against one execution agent and does not test another. AdaCoM (2605.30785) finds the right compression level for a frozen agent's own context depends on that agent's baseline strength, a hint that context artifacts are reader-specific, but it is not a foreign-experience rewriter and reports no held-out reader. HarnessDev (2609.01437) reports self-built harnesses transfer poorly across models. In the home literature, prompt transfer across model sizes has a transferability metric (PANDA 2208.10160) and MePO (2505.09930) claims model-agnostic prompt merits; the question of whether an execution-grounded rewriter is model-agnostic is open. Archived closer_beats_stronger concerned raw memory transfer, not a learned transfer component, and did not separate proximity from capability.
proposals.Abstract: Learned transfer components (rewriters, context augmentation models, memory composers) are trained against one consumer and assumed to serve others. We measure how much of a rewriter's gain survives a change of reader, with the reader manipulated along three separated axes. Two rewriters, both QLoRA adapters on Qwen3-32B, are trained on ALFWorld training games by rejection sampling: candidate rewrites of k=3 retrieved foreign items (expert and EXAONE-4.0-32B banks) are executed by the reader in the loop, and rewrites that turn a verbatim failure into a success are kept as SFT targets; R_A is trained against Qwen3-32B under the standard scaffold, R_B against EXAONE-4.0-32B. Each rewriter is then evaluated on four readers: the training reader, the same backbone under a different scaffold and temperature (proximity), the same backbone in thinking mode (capability at fixed backbone), and the other backbone (backbone at verified matched k=0 success), against verbatim injection at matched consumer tokens, a training-free prompted rewriter, and the rewriter given no retrieved item (memory-absent; detects memorized plans) or items for the wrong task type (mismatched). The transfer fraction is the rewriter's increment on a reader divided by its increment on its training reader, with cluster-bootstrap CIs. A matched-cost arm gives the held-out backbone its own additional bank collected at the rewriter's training GPU-hours. Gate 0 requires each rewriter to beat token-matched verbatim injection on its own reader by 6 net. The claims fail if the foreign-trained rewriter matches the reader-trained one, if the thinking-mode reader keeps less than the other backbone, if the memory-absent rewriter keeps most of the gain, or if the imported rewriter beats self-collection at equal cost.
proposals.Experiments:
- Foreign banks: W_exp (expert) and W_other (EXAONE-4.0-32B successes, collected after serving verification), pooled as the input bank for all rewriter training and evaluation; W_self (Qwen3-32B) is the self-pool control for reader A and the matched-cost arm for reader B is an additional EXAONE bank.
- Readers: A Qwen3-32B standard scaffold non-thinking; A' Qwen3-32B plan-then-act scaffold, T=0.7 (verify k=0 within +/-5 net of A); A'' Qwen3-32B thinking mode (verify k=0 >= 8 net above A); B EXAONE-4.0-32B (verify k=0 within +/-5 net of A; if not, B is reported as a joint backbone-and-capability change and P2 is restricted to A' vs A''). C gpt-oss-120b only if it serves on one A100.
- Rewriter training: for 1,000 training games, 3 candidate rewrites per game from the prompted Qwen3-32B rewriter at T=0.8 (input: task, first observation, k=3 items; output: one plan in the reader's action format), executed by the in-loop reader (3,000 episodes, ~2.5 GPU-h at 20/min), plus the verbatim run (1,000 episodes); keep rewrites where the reader succeeded and verbatim failed, and a 1:1 share of success-success pairs; QLoRA r=32 SFT, one epoch (~1.5 GPU-h). Same recipe for R_B with B in the loop. Rewriter backbone fixed at Qwen3-32B for both, so only the in-loop reader differs.
- Conditions per reader: C0; C_static (Measurement C); C_v3 verbatim; C_vtok verbatim at the k that matches the rewriter's output tokens; C_RA, C_RB the trained rewriters; C_R0 the prompted untrained rewriter; C_RA_empty (rewriter given the task and no item); C_RA_mis (items retrieved for a different task type); for B additionally C_selfcost (B's own bank enlarged by the episode-equivalent of R_A's training GPU-hours, read verbatim).
- Estimands: g(r,cond) = S(r,cond) - S(r,C_static); increment I(R,r) = g(r,R) - g(r,C_vtok); transfer fraction TF(R_A->r) = I(R_A,r)/I(R_A,A) and TF(R_B->r) = I(R_B,r)/I(R_B,B); retained-gain ratio per writer x reader for the verbatim cells; consumer tokens (rewriter output counts as consumer tokens) and episodes/min; training GPU-hours per rewriter.
- Gate 0: I(R_A,A) >= 6 net and I(R_B,B) >= 6 net at 274 x 4 seeds; a rewriter that fails its own reader has nothing to transfer and is reported as a null with the training-free R_0 as the fallback subject for P2.
- Budget: two rewriters ~8 GPU-h; evaluation ~32 cells (headline cells at 4 seeds) ~19k episodes; the rewriter adapter is served on the GPU not serving the reader; about 3 days including bank collection.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations:
- Cheapest first: C_static, then C_R0 (prompted rewriter, no training) before any trained cell.
- Direct injection of the unmodified items at matched tokens (C_vtok) is the comparator for every rewriter cell; C_v3 reported as the cheaper comparator.
- Self-pool control at matched collection cost: W_self for A; for B, C_selfcost converts R_A's training GPU-hours into EXAONE episodes at the measured episodes/GPU-h.
- Memory-absent (C_RA_empty), matched (training reader), mismatched (C_RA_mis and held-out readers) evaluation of each trained component, as the round rules require.
- Named reimplementation: the lightweight rewriter of 2605.30723 as C_RA/C_RB; SkillRevise-style trace-conditioned revision (2606.01139) is named as the untested alternative trainer.
- Ablations: rewriter trained on success-success pairs only (does the contrastive filter matter); rewriter applied at k=1; rewriter with reader identity in the prompt.
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (reader specificity): I(R_B,B) - I(R_A,B) >= 1/3 of I(R_A,A), and symmetrically I(R_A,A) - I(R_B,A) >= the same margin. Falsifier: the foreign-trained rewriter is within the margin of the reader-trained one on either reader, meaning the rewrites are reader-agnostic cleaning. Arm: the (B,C_RA) vs (B,C_RB) and (A,C_RB) vs (A,C_RA) cells at 4 seeds; both rewriters are trained on the same input bank so the cell can produce equality.
- P2 (proximity before capability): TF(R_A->A') >= 0.75, TF(R_A->A'') between 0.5 and 0.75, TF(R_A->B) < 0.5, with the ordering TF(A'') > TF(B) holding at CI level. Falsifier: TF(R_A->B) >= TF(R_A->A'') (the capability change costs more transfer than the backbone change) or TF(R_A->A') < 0.5 (a scaffold change alone breaks the rewriter). Arm: the A', A'' and B rewriter and C_vtok cells.
- P3 (not memorized plans): I(R_A on C_RA_empty, A) <= 1/3 of I(R_A,A). Falsifier: the rewriter with no retrieved item keeps >= 2/3 of its increment, in which case the transfer measured is plan transfer and P1/P2 are re-labelled as such. Arm: C_RA_empty and C_RA_mis for A.
- P4 (matched cost for the held-out backbone): g(B,C_selfcost) >= g(B,C_RA). Falsifier: g(B,C_RA) - g(B,C_selfcost) >= +6 net, i.e. importing the rewriter trained against the other backbone is worth more than the same GPU-hours of B's own experience. Arm: the C_selfcost cell versus (B,C_RA).
- P5 (training buys something): I(R_A,A) - I(R_0,A) >= 1/3 of I(R_A,A). Falsifier: the prompted rewriter is within the margin of the trained one on the training reader. Arm: (A,C_R0) vs (A,C_RA).
- P6 (retained-gain ratio moves with the rewriter): for the W_other bank read by A, the retained-gain ratio under C_RA exceeds the verbatim ratio by >= 0.15. Falsifier: the ratio does not rise or falls. Arm: the (W_other,A) verbatim and C_RA cells with the EXAONE writer reading its own bank as the denominator.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Paired per-game success differences over 274 games x seeds; cluster bootstrap over games with seeds nested for increments, transfer fractions (ratio CIs by bootstrap of numerator and denominator jointly) and the P1 differences of differences; 274 x 4 seeds for the eight headline cells (A and B under C_RA, C_RB, C_vtok, C_selfcost), 274 x 2 elsewhere. Gate 0 at 4 seeds before any held-out cell. Margins as fractions of the Gate-0 increment; one pre-registered headline contrast (P1), P2 secondary, the rest exploratory. Reader temperature 0 except A'; rewriter decoding temperature 0 at evaluation. Consumer tokens per episode include the rewriter's generated plan; training GPU-hours are logged from the runner and converted to episodes at the measured rate for C_selfcost. The reader in the training loop is served on one GPU while the other serves the candidate-rewrite generator, then the QLoRA job runs on one GPU while the other serves the first evaluation cells.
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: All queries via tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (s2=ok hf=ok). (1) recent, closest named method: 'model-conditioned skill rewriter adapt skills to target backbone transfer to held-out model' -> 2605.30723 (rewriter per backbone, no held-out reader), SkillRevise 2606.01139 (claims cross-model transfer of revised skills, no fraction reported), 2605.23899, Skill-R1 2605.09359, SkillX 2604.04804; the two nearest cards make opposite predictions and neither reports a transfer fraction or a matched-cost self-collection arm. (2) recent: 'context augmentation model execution feedback transfer to different execution agent backbone' -> AdaCoM 2605.30785 (verified with s2cli paper; reader-strength-dependent compression for the agent's own context), CLEAR 2604.07487, HarnessDev 2609.01437 (harnesses transfer poorly across models), Harness-Bench 2605.27922; none trains a component against one reader and scores it on another. (3) home: 'prompt optimization transferability across target language models optimized on one model evaluated on another' (answered after a rate-limit delay by the same channel) -> MePO 2505.09930 (model-agnostic prompt merits), PANDA 2208.10160 (prompt transfer across model sizes with a transferability metric), 2305.13954, GReaTer 2412.09722; these ask the home-vocabulary question for static prompts and do not cover execution-grounded rewriting of retrieved trajectories or a self-collection cost arm. (4) recent: 'reconstruct retrieved experience conditioned on current state agent cross-model transfer' -> MemHarness 2607.28272, 2608.26730, 2607.13884; no held-out reader. No paper found that reports the fraction of a learned rewriter's gain retained by a held-out reader with proximity and capability separated.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: Rejection sampling may yield only a few hundred contrastive pairs, so the adapter can underfit and fail Gate 0; the fallback subject is the prompted rewriter R_0, which still supports P2 and P4 but not P1/P5. The rewriter backbone is Qwen3-32B for both R_A and R_B, so R_A has a same-family advantage on A that is a feature of the design (the in-loop reader is the only difference) but limits generality across rewriter backbones. If EXAONE-4.0-32B does not serve, B is unavailable and only the within-backbone proximity and capability readers remain; if gpt-oss-120b serves, it replaces B as a backbone change with a larger capability gap and P2 is re-stated accordingly. Thinking mode multiplies tokens and halves throughput; token-matched comparisons for A'' use that reader's own C_vtok. Transfer fractions are ratios and are unstable when the denominator is small, hence Gate 0. ALFWorld's six procedures make the rewriter's job narrow; a second domain is out of budget.
proposals.Addresses gap: G17 (learned transfer components not tested on held-out backbones, capability gaps or scaffolds) as the primary target; G20 (adaptation cost never matched against plain retrieval or self-collection) through C_vtok and C_selfcost; G18 through the retained-gain ratio under the rewriter.
proposals.Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: the in-scope list names a model-conditioned skill rewriter (2605.30723) as a baseline to reimplement and Q5 asks whether a rewriter learned against one reader transfers; this idea supplies what neither states, the transfer fraction as the estimand, its ordering by proximity versus capability with the reader manipulated on three separated axes, and the equal-GPU-hour self-collection comparison for the held-out backbone. Digest card: 2605.30723 claims skills must be adapted per backbone and trains a rewriter per backbone; this idea claims the rewriter itself is reader-specific by a measured fraction, that a memory-absent rewriter must not keep the gain, and that importing it loses to self-collection at equal cost, none of which the card tests; the conflicting card 2606.01139 claims cross-model transfer of revised skills without a fraction, and this design arbitrates between them. Archived closer_beats_stronger measured raw memory transfer with proximity and capability confounded; here the transferred object is a trained component and the two axes are separated within one backbone.
